correctness.rationale: For every j including the half-period seam, the antipodal edge pair consists of a_j+d_j and -a_j+d_j. Equality forces Re(conj(a_j)d_j)=0; equality across pairs then forces the same |d_j|=t. At t=0 this is a translation, while at t>0 the perpendicular differences are exactly the signed choice in the Finding. They integrate to a periodic c if and only if their sum is zero. For m a power of two, Phi_{2m}=x^m+1 is the minimal polynomial, too large in degree to divide a nonzero sign polynomial of length m; this includes n=4. Otherwise write m=qd for odd d>1. In the proposed block signs, -zeta^q is a nontrivial d-th root and its geometric sum is zero. This proves the classification and existence for all stated n, not only sampled orders. For geometry near t=0, all oriented edge/other-vertex determinants are strictly positive at the regular polygon, so their simultaneous positivity persists and all ordered edges bound its strictly convex hull; this is a global convexity justification, not just a check of local turns. The shifts are O_n(t) and all nonopposite vertex distances retain the strict gap below one from cos(pi/n); the fixed antipodal vectors have length one and vertex distances determine the hull's diameter. Pythagoras gives the exact common side length; Taylor expansion gives the stated quadratic gain. The global classification is algebraic only, and power-of-two rigidity fixes labeled vectors rather than merely their lengths. Proof replay is given by these identities; the frozen checker was inspected, not executed, and finite tests are not needed for the universal proof.

The distinct supported claims are the full equal-side classification for all paired translations, the restricted dyadic rigidity, and the paired-vector construction also when 4 divides n and n has an odd factor. value.rationale: Exactly freezing the original active diameter vectors defines a natural restricted nonlinear model at the regular even polygon. The complete equal-side parameterization and the correct restricted rigidity/ascent boundary tell when those constraints suffice to prevent a perimeter improvement, and give an exact feasible direction family when they do not. This is meaningful also for orders divisible by four, where the earlier radial witness cannot preserve the vectors. It does not claim unrestricted dyadic optimality or new global perimeter maxima.
